source: You’ll notice that the top 3—bone, desert, and dust—make up 43% of all usage, and there is a pretty quick drop-off after that with a long tail of rarer choices.
claim: For "dry", the three most-used nouns — bone (174 occurrences), desert (169) and dust (135) — make up 42.7% of the 1,119 occurrences summed across the 30 nouns shown in its chart.

source: “Cucumber” (or as I learned that it sometimes was referred to as cowcumber) doesn’t even crack the top ten in usage for any other adjective.
claim: Cucumber is the most-used noun only for "cool" (298 occurrences); in its other adjectives it ranks 15th (calm, 4) and 17th (green, 3), never inside the top ten.

source: The scale tips towards the defenseless side with the highest usage coming with “as helpless as a child”
claim: "Helpless" is the adjective that "child" is most used with: 112 occurrences, ahead of innocent (95) and weak (75).

source: But child is only the second most-used noun for both of these adjectives, trailing the less evolved form: baby
claim: For both helpless and innocent, baby is the most-used noun (153 and 143 occurrences, rank 1) and child the second most-used (112 and 95, rank 2).

Each adjective's chart labels its most-used noun and that noun's count, which is the adjective's highest-count vehicle in the data: white–snow 924, good–death 912, cold–ice 855, hard–stone 771, still–statue 728, cool–cucumber 298, broad–ox 12 and real–memory 8 among them.
